article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 50% Indica / 50% Sativa
Genetics: Blockberry / Super Boof × Tropicana Cherry
Breeder: Grow More Fire Genetics
THC Content: 22–28%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Cherry, blood orange, tropical fruit, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Potentially high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Super Buff Cherry is the kind of modern cannabis strain that announces itself before anyone has taken a hit. Proper flower can display almost theatrical shades of purple, pink, burgundy, and green beneath a dense coating of trichomes, while the aroma pushes bright cherry and citrus into the foreground. Yet its popularity is not built on appearance alone. The selected Super Buff Cherry #26 combines exceptionally vigorous growth, an unusually fast eight-week flowering cycle, strong resin production, and a balanced high that avoids being locked completely into either the indica or sativa category. The original breeder created the cultivar by crossing the celebrated Blockberry/Super Boof cut with Tropicana Cherry and selected phenotype #26 from a hunt involving 33 plants. That keeper became the reference cut most growers mean when discussing Super Buff Cherry today.
Genetics and Lineage

The family tree contains an unusually concentrated dose of cherry and Tropicana genetics. On one side sits the Blockberry cut commonly known as Super Boof, descended from Black Cherry Punch × Tropicana Cookies . On the other is Tropicana Cherry, bred from Tropicana Cookies × Cherry Cookies F3. The breeder specifically documents these parents and notes the repeated presence of Tropicana Cookies and cherry-oriented genetics throughout the pedigree. Rather than producing a muddled fruit hybrid, that repetition appears to reinforce the characteristics enthusiasts now associate with the cultivar: saturated coloration, citrus-heavy aromatics, ripe red-fruit notes, and generous resin.

Phenotype selection was equally important. Thirty-three seedlings were evaluated before #26 was retained as the keeper. According to the breeder’s cultivation notes, this plant stood out for vigorous vegetative growth, thick lateral branching, rapid transition into bloom, early purple coloration, dense frost coverage, and a tropical-fruit aroma. Flowers can begin showing strong purple expression by roughly the second week of bloom, well before final ripening. This makes #26 more than simply one random plant from the cross; it is the selection around which Super Buff Cherry’s modern reputation largely developed.

The genetic balance also explains why the cultivar resists simplistic classification. Its growth can be vigorous and expansive, while the finished marijuana combines mental uplift with an increasingly relaxed physical tone. The breeder describes the keeper as a true 50/50 hybrid and has continued using Super Buff Cherry #26 as breeding stock in newer lines, demonstrating its importance beyond the original release.
Effects and Experience

The first portion of the experience tends to be bright and socially engaging. A noticeable cerebral shift can develop quickly, bringing an upbeat mood, increased interest in conversation, and a slightly playful quality that works particularly well around music, friends, or low-pressure creative activities. Thoughts remain relatively active rather than becoming immediately foggy, which separates this cultivar from many heavily sedating purple strains. Moderate servings can feel functional despite substantial THC content.

Physical relaxation arrives more gradually. As the initial mental lift settles, tension may seem less prominent and the body develops a comfortable weight without necessarily becoming immobilized. This middle ground is one of Super Buff Cherry’s strongest characteristics: enough stimulation to remain interesting, but enough physical calm to make the experience suitable for unwinding. Some licensed flower releases characterize the effect as sociable, giggly, hungry, and relaxed, which closely matches the balanced nature expected from its genetics.

The breeder reports roughly 26% THC for the selected #26 plant, placing it firmly in high-potency territory. Individual commercial harvests can vary, so the laboratory result on a particular package remains more useful than a universal strain percentage. High amounts may turn the energetic beginning into mental distraction or anxiety, especially for inexperienced consumers. Dry mouth, dry eyes, impaired coordination, short-term memory disruption, and altered perception are also established effects associated with THC-rich cannabis.
Medical Benefits

The balanced progression gives Super Buff Cherry practical appeal among medical marijuana consumers who want relaxation without immediately feeling heavily sedated. Its combination of mood elevation, appetite stimulation, and physical calm may make it attractive for people using cannabis while dealing with stress, reduced appetite, or persistent discomfort. Still, strain reputation should not be confused with clinical evidence. There are no controlled studies demonstrating that Super Buff Cherry specifically treats pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical disorder.

Research on cannabis more broadly provides a clearer perspective. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes evidence suggesting modest benefits from cannabis or cannabinoids for some chronic pain conditions, although improvements are generally limited and side effects must be considered. Research remains highly dependent on cannabinoid formulation, dosage, delivery method, and the condition being studied. A high-THC flower cultivar cannot automatically be expected to reproduce results obtained with standardized medicinal products.

Anxiety deserves particular caution because cannabis effects can move in opposite directions depending on dose and individual sensitivity. Someone may experience temporary relaxation at a modest amount while becoming anxious, fearful, or panicky after consuming too much THC. Anyone using weed for ongoing medical symptoms should therefore consider cannabinoid concentration, medications, personal tolerance, and professional medical advice rather than assuming the strain name predicts therapeutic response.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Aromatic intensity is arguably the cultivar’s defining feature. The first impression often resembles ripe cherry mixed with orange peel and tropical fruit, followed by berry sweetness and a light floral quality. Breaking apart a resinous flower can release considerably more citrus, sometimes approaching blood orange, tangerine, or grapefruit. Beneath that fruit sits enough earthy gas and spice to prevent the profile from becoming purely sugary. The breeder describes the selected #26 phenotype as carrying a strong tropical-fruit smell and taste.

Limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and myrcene frequently appear prominently in tested commercial examples, although terpene composition changes with cultivation and harvest. A licensed medical-cannabis producer currently lists those three among the cultivar’s principal terpenes and characterizes its aroma around cherry, citrus, and gas. Other batches have also shown linalool and additional minor terpenes, reinforcing why no single terpene chart should be treated as universal.

The flavor carries much of that aromatic brightness into the smoke or vapor. Cherry and sweet citrus dominate early, followed by tropical fruit and berry before a slightly spicy, earthy finish develops. Lower-temperature vaporization can emphasize the sharper fruit components, while combustion tends to make the pepper and gas more apparent. For consumers who enjoy Tropicana Cookies-style marijuana, Super Buff Cherry can feel familiar while adding considerably more cherry richness and visual intensity.
Growing Information

Super Buff Cherry #26 is unusually well documented by its breeder compared with many clone-driven modern cultivars. Vegetative growth is described as vigorous and easy to manage, with thick lateral branches capable of forming numerous productive tops. The natural branching pattern makes the plant particularly suitable for topping, low-stress training, and trellising. Instead of forcing a narrow central cola upward, growers can spread those branches into a relatively flat canopy that takes efficient advantage of indoor lighting.

Flowering moves quickly. Transition begins rapidly after the light cycle changes, and visible purple pigmentation can develop by approximately day 14. Buds then gain density and resin quickly as maturity approaches. Most importantly, the breeder identifies the keeper as a genuine 56-day finisher, giving growers an unusually short eight-week flowering window for marijuana with this level of visual and aromatic complexity. Mature flowers are described as pink, dense, heavily frosted, and strongly tropical in aroma.

Dense flowers require competent humidity control late in bloom. Good airflow around the canopy and sensible humidity levels help limit moisture accumulation as colas thicken. The cultivar’s strong lateral branches can support substantial flower development, although trellising may still be beneficial under intensive lighting. Exact yield figures are not published for the original #26 cut, so claims promising a fixed number of grams per square meter should be treated cautiously. What is documented is strong vegetative vigor, multiple productive tops, rapid flowering, substantial frost, and unusually good resin performance—the breeder specifically notes that the plant washes well, making it attractive for hash and solventless concentrate production.
FAQ
What strains make Super Buff Cherry?

The original cultivar combines the Blockberry/Super Boof cut with Tropicana Cherry. Super Boof is Black Cherry Punch × Tropicana Cookies, while the Tropicana Cherry parent is Tropicana Cookies × Cherry Cookies F3.
Who bred Super Buff Cherry?

Super Buff Cherry was created by Grow More Fire Genetics, also associated with the Grow More Stress Less name. Phenotype #26 was selected as the keeper after the breeder evaluated 33 plants from the cross.
Is Super Buff Cherry indica or sativa?

The breeder describes the #26 keeper as a 50/50 hybrid. Its experience reflects that balance reasonably well, beginning with cerebral uplift and sociability before developing into a calmer and more relaxed physical state.
How strong is Super Buff Cherry?

The breeder reports approximately 26% THC for Super Buff Cherry #26. Actual commercial flower varies according to growing conditions and harvest, so current laboratory testing should always take precedence over an average published for the cultivar.
How long does Super Buff Cherry take to flower?

The original #26 keeper is notably fast, reaching harvest maturity at approximately 56 days, or eight weeks of flowering. Plant development and trichome maturity should still be evaluated before harvest rather than relying exclusively on the calendar.
Final Thoughts on Super Buff Cherry

Super Buff Cherry captures several traits that modern cannabis breeders pursue simultaneously but rarely combine this successfully: exceptional color, heavy resin, loud aroma, vigorous growth, respectable potency, and a short flowering period. The repeated Tropicana and cherry ancestry gives the cultivar a recognizable core of citrus and red fruit, while Super Boof adds enough depth, resin, and structural strength to keep the plant from feeling like an aroma-first novelty.

For consumers, its strongest attraction is the combination of cherry, citrus, tropical fruit, and subtle gas paired with a balanced cerebral-to-physical high. Growers gain something equally valuable: an energetic plant with strong lateral branching that can finish in roughly eight weeks and produce exceptionally frosty, colorful flowers. The #26 keeper selected by Grow More Fire Genetics remains the reference expression of Super Buff Cherry, and its continued use in newer breeding projects suggests that its influence on contemporary marijuana genetics is likely to extend well beyond the original cross.
